tomato_bacterial_spot.how_to_handle_infected_leaves: Prune and remove infected leaves during dry weather to prevent spreading. Destroy or deeply bury the infected plant debris; do not compost them.
tomato_bacterial_spot.how_to_irrigate: Avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation which splashes bacteria onto healthy leaves. Use drip irrigation or furrow irrigation to keep foliage completely dry. Water early in the morning.
tomato_bacterial_spot.chemicals_for_treatment: Copper-based fungicides/bactericides combined with Mancozeb. Streptomycin sulfate or Kasugamycin can be used in severe cases where permitted.
tomato_bacterial_spot.locally_available_chemicals_in_india: Kocide (Copper Hydroxide), Blitox (Copper Oxychloride), Indofil M-45 (Mancozeb), Streptocycline (Streptomycin + Tetracycline).
tomato_bacterial_spot.precautions_to_prevent_recurrence: Use certified disease-free seeds and transplants. Practice a 2-3 year crop rotation with non-solanaceous crops. Clean and sanitize tools, stakes, and equipment regularly.
tomato_bacterial_spot.professional_consultation_disclaimer: Chemical recommendations can vary based on local regulations and resistance patterns. Please also refer to and consult with agricultural professionals or local extension offices nearby before applying chemical treatments.

tomato_early_blight.how_to_handle_infected_leaves: Remove lower infected leaves early in the season to prevent the fungus from climbing up the plant. Burn or dispose of debris far away from the plot.
tomato_early_blight.how_to_irrigate: Apply water directly to the soil using drip lines or soaker hoses. Avoid wetting the leaves, as the fungal spores require moisture to germinate.
tomato_early_blight.chemicals_for_treatment: Chlorothalonil, Mancozeb, Azoxystrobin, Pyraclostrobin, or Difenoconazole.
tomato_early_blight.precautions_to_prevent_recurrence: Maintain excellent plant spacing for air circulation. Stake and cage tomato plants up off the ground. Mulch the soil surface to prevent soil-borne spores from splashing onto lower leaves.
tomato_early_blight.professional_consultation_disclaimer: Chemical recommendations can vary based on local regulations and resistance patterns. Please also refer to and consult with agricultural professionals or local extension offices nearby before applying chemical treatments.

tomato_healthy.how_to_handle_infected_leaves: No infected leaves present. Maintain standard pruning of lower yellowing or old non-productive leaves to improve aeration.
tomato_healthy.how_to_irrigate: Provide consistent moisture (approx. 1-1.5 inches per week) using drip irrigation. Avoid waterlogging or extreme dry-to-wet moisture swings to prevent blossom end rot.
tomato_healthy.chemicals_for_treatment: None required. Preventative bio-fungicides like Trichoderma viride or Pseudomonas fluorescens can be applied to maintain health.
tomato_healthy.locally_available_chemicals_in_india: Bio-products like Sanjivani (Trichoderma), Sudozone (Pseudomonas), or light Neem Oil sprays for general pest deterrence.
tomato_healthy.precautions_to_prevent_recurrence: Continue robust crop rotation, weed management, and maintain optimum soil nutrition based on periodic soil testing.
tomato_healthy.professional_consultation_disclaimer: To maintain high yields and ideal crop health, please also refer to and consult with agricultural professionals or local extension offices nearby for customized crop schedules.

tomato_late_blight.how_to_handle_infected_leaves: Highly contagious. Immediately bag and remove the entire infected plant if symptoms are widespread, or carefully strip infected leaves. Do not compost; burn or bury deeply.
tomato_late_blight.how_to_irrigate: Strictly use drip irrigation. Ensure watering happens in the morning so any accidental moisture evaporates quickly. Minimize humidity within the plant canopy.
tomato_late_blight.chemicals_for_treatment: Metalaxyl combined with Mancozeb, Cymoxanil, Dimethomorph, or Propamocarb.
tomato_late_blight.locally_available_chemicals_in_india: Ridomil Gold (Metalaxyl + Mancozeb), Curzate (Cymoxanil + Mancozeb), Acrobat (Dimethomorph), Sectin (Fenamidone + Mancozeb).
tomato_late_blight.precautions_to_prevent_recurrence: Plant resistant tomato varieties. Avoid planting tomatoes near potatoes. Destroy any volunteer tomato or potato plants in the off-season.
tomato_late_blight.professional_consultation_disclaimer: Chemical recommendations can vary based on local regulations and resistance patterns. Please also refer to and consult with agricultural professionals or local extension offices nearby before applying chemical treatments.

tomato_leaf_mold.how_to_handle_infected_leaves: Remove infected leaves carefully to avoid releasing thousands of airborne spores. Improve ventilation inside greenhouses or polyhouses.
tomato_leaf_mold.how_to_irrigate: Water early in the day directly at the root zone. Avoid overhead irrigation completely to keep relative humidity below 85%.
tomato_leaf_mold.chemicals_for_treatment: Chlorothalonil, Mancozeb, Difenoconazole, or copper fungicides.
tomato_leaf_mold.precautions_to_prevent_recurrence: Increase spacing between plants and prune lower branches to enhance airflow. Grow tomatoes in well-ventilated structures. Use resistant cultivars.
tomato_leaf_mold.professional_consultation_disclaimer: Chemical recommendations can vary based on local regulations and resistance patterns. Please also refer to and consult with agricultural professionals or local extension offices nearby before applying chemical treatments.

tomato_septoria_leaf_spot.how_to_handle_infected_leaves: Prune off severely spotted lower leaves as soon as they appear. Wash hands and sanitize tools before touching healthy plants.
tomato_septoria_leaf_spot.how_to_irrigate: Use drip hoses or ground watering systems. Avoid overhead watering since spores are easily spread via water droplets and splashing.
tomato_septoria_leaf_spot.chemicals_for_treatment: Chlorothalonil, Mancozeb, Copper Fungicides, or Azoxystrobin.
tomato_septoria_leaf_spot.locally_available_chemicals_in_india: Indofil M-45 (Mancozeb), Kavach (Chlorothalonil), Kocide (Copper Hydroxide), Amistar (Azoxystrobin).
tomato_septoria_leaf_spot.precautions_to_prevent_recurrence: Eliminate solanaceous weeds (like nightshade) around the field. Practice strict crop rotation. Mulch thoroughly around the base of the tomato plants.
tomato_septoria_leaf_spot.professional_consultation_disclaimer: Chemical recommendations can vary based on local regulations and resistance patterns. Please also refer to and consult with agricultural professionals or local extension offices nearby before applying chemical treatments.

spider_mites_two_spotted_spider_mite.how_to_handle_infected_leaves: Remove heavily infested leaves or sections showing severe webbing and yellow stippling. Bag and discard them away from the field.
spider_mites_two_spotted_spider_mite.how_to_irrigate: Ensure the crop is not water-stressed, as dry and dusty conditions accelerate mite reproduction. Overhead misting can sometimes physically knock mites off, but balances with fungal risks.
spider_mites_two_spotted_spider_mite.locally_available_chemicals_in_india: Oberon (Spiromesifen), Omite (Propargite), Vertimec or Abacin (Abamectin), Maiden (Hexythiazox).
spider_mites_two_spotted_spider_mite.precautions_to_prevent_recurrence: Keep field borders free of weeds that harbor mites. Keep dust down on farm pathways. Encourage or release natural predators like predatory mites, lacewings, or ladybugs.
spider_mites_two_spotted_spider_mite.professional_consultation_disclaimer: Chemical recommendations can vary based on local regulations and resistance patterns. Please also refer to and consult with agricultural professionals or local extension offices nearby before applying chemical treatments.

tomato_target_spot.how_to_handle_infected_leaves: Pick off affected leaves with concentric target-like rings to minimize spore production. Dispose of all infected crop residues after harvest.
tomato_target_spot.how_to_irrigate: Irrigate at the base of the plant using drip systems. Keep the canopy as dry as possible to reduce the high humidity periods required by this fungus.
tomato_target_spot.chemicals_for_treatment: Azoxystrobin, Chlorothalonil, Corynespora-effective systemic fungicides like Boscalid or Fluopyram.
tomato_target_spot.precautions_to_prevent_recurrence: Maintain open plant canopy with wide spacing and proper staking. Avoid planting continuous solanaceous crops. Control weed hosts.
tomato_target_spot.professional_consultation_disclaimer: Chemical recommendations can vary based on local regulations and resistance patterns. Please also refer to and consult with agricultural professionals or local extension offices nearby before applying chemical treatments.

tomato_mosaic_virus.how_to_handle_infected_leaves: Do not just remove leaves. Immediately pull up and discard the entire infected plant including roots. Burn or deeply bury them. Do not touch healthy plants after handling infected ones.
tomato_mosaic_virus.how_to_irrigate: Irrigate normally via drip. Avoid physical contact with water hoses or moving through wet fields, as the virus spreads mechanically via clothing and tools.
tomato_mosaic_virus.chemicals_for_treatment: No chemical treatment is effective against viral pathogens. Spraying skim milk or antiviral solutions on tools can help reduce mechanical transmission.
tomato_mosaic_virus.locally_available_chemicals_in_india: No curative chemical available. Preventive viricides or disinfectants like Trisodium Phosphate (TSP) or Sodium Hypochlorite for cleaning tools.
tomato_mosaic_virus.precautions_to_prevent_recurrence: Grow certified virus-free seeds or resistant varieties (look for ToMV resistance). Wash hands with soap and water/milk before handling plants. Prohibit smoking/tobacco handling near the farm.
tomato_mosaic_virus.professional_consultation_disclaimer: Viral diseases can spread rapidly and devastate crops. Please also refer to and consult with agricultural professionals or local extension offices nearby for testing and containment advice.

tomato_yellow_leaf_curl_virus.how_to_handle_infected_leaves: Pull out and destroy entire infected plants immediately to reduce the reservoir for whiteflies. Place them in plastic bags before removal to avoid spreading vector insects.
tomato_yellow_leaf_curl_virus.how_to_irrigate: Standard drip irrigation. Maintain optimal water supply to prevent stress, which makes plants more susceptible to vector damage.
tomato_yellow_leaf_curl_virus.chemicals_for_treatment: No chemical cure for the virus itself. Treatment focuses strictly on controlling the vector (Whiteflies) using systemic insecticides like Imidacloprid, Acetamiprid, or Thiamethoxam.
tomato_yellow_leaf_curl_virus.locally_available_chemicals_in_india: Confidor (Imidacloprid), Pride or Manik (Acetamiprid), Actara (Thiamethoxam), Pegasus (Diafenthiuron). Neem oil can be used as an organic deterrent.
tomato_yellow_leaf_curl_virus.precautions_to_prevent_recurrence: Use insect-proof net meshes (40-mesh or finer) in nurseries/greenhouses. Use yellow sticky cards to monitor whitefly populations. Plant TYLCV-resistant hybrids.
tomato_yellow_leaf_curl_virus.professional_consultation_disclaimer: Vector management is critical to halting virus spread. Please also refer to and consult with agricultural professionals or local extension offices nearby before applying chemical treatments.
